Regarding the statute from the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) mentioned in the text: This provision establishes employer sanctions that make it illegal for employers to knowingly hire, recruit, or refer for a fee individuals who are not authorized to work in the United States. The legal implications of violating this provision include significant civil fines and potential criminal penalties. Employers are required to verify the identity and employment authorization of all employees hired after November 6, 1986, typically by completing Form I-9. Failure to comply with these verification requirements or knowingly hiring unauthorized workers can result in substantial financial penalties and, in cases of pattern or practice violations, criminal charges.
